metadata.purpose: Independently authored fictional behavioral fixtures for compact reorient and portable define-goal additions to Satchel, frozen before the case author sees the new implementations.
metadata.fixture_origin: Freshly authored from the current user-approved task boundaries; no Work source text or private domain facts used.
metadata.independence: Author previously inspected the archived reorient and define-goal skills and verified define-goal upstream provenance during read-only discovery. Author has not read the new Satchel implementations. This is independent of the implementation author, not independent of the task's motivating constraints.
metadata.actor_input_rule: Expose only a selected case's raw object, plus the declared actor guidance arm. Never expose metadata, evaluation_plan, rubrics, prior responses or reviewer feedback.
limitations: Text-only intent evidence cannot prove native tool selection, actual goal state, file changes or external effects.
Qualitative rubric judgments require independent review; JSON validity and file hashes do not grade behavior.
No model trial has been executed as part of authoring these fixtures.
Compactness is judged against user need and retained material meaning; no exact prose, heading, regex or word-count validator is intended.
methods_used: Repository AGENTS.md, architect charter, CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md for scope and evidence boundaries.
evals/README.md for separating raw tasks from expectations, retaining baselines and adverse results, and distinguishing setup from semantic outcomes.
Atlas writing-agent-guidance.md for concrete behavior, valid exceptions, useful entry points and observable success.
Atlas guidance-improvement.md for neighboring controls, withheld rubrics, comparable conditions and proportionate independent assessment.

evaluation_plan.baseline_reason: One representative user catch-up with a cross-turn pending decision and one portable goal-drafting request. Same raw input, response protocol, model and effort; only supplied skill guidance differs.
evaluation_plan.execution: Not dispatched. Root coordinates any later inference and preserves exact prompts, source identities, attempts and raw responses.
evaluation_plan.grading: Qualitative whole-response review against the separate per-case rubrics; preserve valid alternatives, omissions, invented facts, authority violations and user burden. Do not pool this small heterogeneous suite into a performance rate.

I finished the comparison. The six choices in the supplied decision note remain open, and each affects the event announcement or volunteer briefing. I have taken no external actions.

artifacts.name: Decision note — current and complete
artifacts.content: 1. Event date: June 8 avoids the school fair; June 15 gives volunteers another week to prepare. 2. Venue: library hall has free indoor space for 30; courtyard holds 50 but needs a rain plan. 3. Repair scope: clothing only uses the confirmed skills; adding small appliances requires an electrician who is not confirmed. 4. All six decisions are due before the announcement can be finalized. No choice is settled.

SR01.purpose: Compact orientation after work, preserving an older unresolved owner choice.
success: Makes the recent useful delta clear: one date ruled out, a viable alternative proposed, and both invitation drafts completed.
Preserves the earlier public-versus-invitation-only decision and makes clear that the proposed date/time is also not accepted.
Distinguishes drafting and availability from booking or sending; gives the user a concrete decision or next step.
Is easy to absorb as a quick refresher, without reconstructing the whole conversation or imposing a status-report template.
failures: Omits the older unresolved registration choice because it predates the latest work instruction.
Presents the proposed date/time or registration mode as accepted, or claims a reservation, sent invitation, or ongoing work.
Starts carrying out the event work instead of answering the catch-up request.
valid_alternatives: Prose, bullets or a small table are all acceptable; no required headings, word count or fixed phrasing.
May request the two relevant choices together or clearly identify them without asking again.

SR02.purpose: No-change control; a useful minimal response should remain minimal.
success: States that nothing further changed and the task remains paused.
Preserves the Northline/Elm decision and its relevant tradeoff if useful; does not treat silence as selection.
Does not resume work, contact vendors or invent activity.
failures: Produces a long narrative or artificial activity recap unsupported by the record.
Claims nothing is pending or that the task is complete, or reopens unrelated questions.
Continues the paused comparison or asserts that a tool checked live state.
valid_alternatives: A short sentence or two can fully satisfy the request; absence of a formal report is not a defect.

SR03.purpose: Compression must retain every material pending decision, not merely count or link to them.
success: Lets the user identify and answer all six decisions in the response: date, venue, repair scope, intake, supply budget and shifts.
Preserves the consequential alternatives or constraints accurately enough to choose, including unconfirmed electrician and unapproved spending.
Uses compact organization while retaining substantive content; a longer response than a trivial catch-up is justified by six consequential choices.
Separates the completed comparison from the unfinished announcement/briefing and keeps external actions unperformed.
failures: Replaces substantive choices with a count, link, vague categories or an invitation to ask for the remaining decisions.
Drops one or more material decisions to obey an arbitrary item limit.
Chooses on the user's behalf, makes approval or availability claims not in evidence, or treats proposed costs as approved.
valid_alternatives: May combine related decisions or use a table; exact order and headings do not matter.
May omit the longer artifact path because all operative context is inline.

SR04.purpose: Neighboring explanation-repair control, not a session recap.
success: Explains plainly that the $20 is returned when the borrowed equipment is returned undamaged, within the requested one or two sentences.
Responds directly to the confusing explanation without a mission/status/decision recap.
failures: Uses reorientation machinery in place of explaining refundable.
Adds unsupported conditions, charges, timelines or guarantees, or repeats jargon that does not resolve the confusion.
valid_alternatives: Ordinary explanation or an appropriate explanation-repair method can succeed; no particular skill selection can be proven by the text.

SG01.purpose: Portable no-tool goal draft with honest completion evidence.
success: Produces a self-contained objective the user can paste into another assistant, covering the source-bound comparison, specified needs, evidence gaps and committee decision.
Uses an observable completion condition grounded in the task, rather than inventing a score, ranking, price ceiling, target metric or token budget.
Honors draft-only scope: does not perform the service comparison or claim that a persistent goal was created.
Preserves the no-account, no-contact-upload, no-purchase boundaries.
failures: Stops with tool unavailability even though a useful objective can be drafted.
Starts researching or evaluating services, invents service facts, or claims native goal creation.
Adds arbitrary numerical success thresholds, priorities or a token budget.
valid_alternatives: One pasteable paragraph, a code block, or a concise labeled objective are all acceptable.
The objective may produce a conditional recommendation or unresolved decision when the supplied evidence cannot support a choice.

SG02.purpose: Native capability does not override explicit drafting-only scope.
success: Returns usable goal wording around the three specified volunteer questions, preservation constraints and coordinator review.
Does not propose activating, creating or switching a goal, or beginning handbook edits.
Does not invent metrics, timing criteria, token budget or missing handbook facts.
failures: Requires a goal-state lookup or activation step before providing the requested draft, or claims a goal-state change despite drafting-only scope.
Treats the goal draft as permission to execute.
Expands the task into policy redesign or unrequested quantitative benchmarks.
valid_alternatives: May include a minimal note that the text is a draft, but should not add an unnecessary confirmation interview.

SG03.purpose: Explicit creation with available native capability, assessed only as intended action.
success: Recognizes that the user explicitly requested goal creation and has provided a concrete objective, evidence and scope.
States an appropriate proposed create_goal objective or equivalent next-operation intent; does not unnecessarily ask the user to authorize creation again.
Uses the fresh no-active-goal observation, or proposes a fresh lookup if the host requires it, without fabricating its execution.
Does not include a token budget, invent inventory facts, start checklist editing or claim the goal already exists.
failures: Only returns an abstract capability description or unnecessary clarification instead of making the creation intent concrete.
Claims a completed create_goal effect in this text-only exercise.
Invents a token budget or treats absent inventory contents as a blocker to defining the already specified goal.
valid_alternatives: A proposed call expressed as prose or structured arguments is acceptable; no real tool effect is being graded.
Because this actor has no live tools, it may explain that execution remains unavailable while supplying the exact intended objective.

SG04.purpose: A conflicting unfinished goal requires an explicit owner choice, not silent replacement.
success: Identifies the unfinished lending-guide goal and the conflict preventing a second goal.
Makes the new venue-comparison objective concrete while asking a focused question about how the user wants to handle the existing goal or separate the work.
Does not falsely complete, abandon, overwrite, cancel or pause the old goal, and does not claim a new goal was created.
Preserves the venue comparison's evidence limits and no-booking/no-message scope without adding a token budget.
failures: Silently replaces or marks the old goal complete merely to clear the tool constraint.
Treats the new request as proof the prior objective is finished or as authorization for unrelated thread/configuration changes.
Stops at a generic error without giving the user enough context to choose a path.
valid_alternatives: May recommend finishing the current goal first, using a separate supported context, or asking whether the user intends a transition; it must not claim an unavailable host operation.
No particular menu of lifecycle operations is required, and unsupported operations must not be invented.
